hypothesisChecks.title: Classical tower trace
hypothesisChecks.statement: Let E/Q have a modular parametrization X_0(N)→E, let K be imaginary quadratic with every prime dividing N split, and let p be a prime not dividing N. If y_(p^n) is the associated point and H_infinity the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension inside K[p^infinity], some n≥0 has Tr_(K[p^infinity]/H_infinity)(y_(p^n)) non-torsion. The trace is the finite torsion-subgroup sum on a point of finite orbit. Cornut also proves infinite-dimensional character-projected span for any nonzero modular abelian quotient of J_0(N). Ordinary reduction, p odd, the discriminant exclusions and residual hypotheses belong to a narrower Iwasawa application, not to this geometric statement.

sources.locator: Introduction main theorem, pp.1–2; §4 Theorem A, pp.20–21
sources.match: Some finite conductor has an infinite-order tower trace; the stronger modular quotient statement does not assume ordinary reduction.

acceptance: Do not replace the tower trace by y_1 or the trace from K[1] to K.
Retain Howard/HE.8 application hypotheses when importing the narrower existing target; do not broaden that target in this packet.

hypothesisChecks.title: CV tower, conductor and fixed torsion character
hypothesisChecks.statement: F is totally real, K/F is CM, P is a finite prime with residue characteristic p. O_C=O_F+C O_K, G(n)=Pic(O_(P^n))=Gal(K[P^n]/K), and G_infinity is their inverse limit. Its finite torsion subgroup G_0 has quotient Z_p of rank [F_P:Q_p]; G_2 is the image of A_F^× and identifies with Pic(O_F). For n large enough that G_0 injects into G(n), fix chi_0 on G_0 with chi_0 omega=1 on G_2. P(n,chi_0) consists of the characters restricting to chi_0 and not factoring through G(n−1). Its conductor is the O_F ring-class conductor, not the generally smaller O_K Hecke conductor. No rank-one tower assumption over general F is made.

sources.locator: §1.1 equations (1),(3), ring-class conventions and P(n,chi_0), pp.3–6; §2.1 Corollary 2.2, p.21; Lemma 2.8, p.23

hypothesisChecks.title: CV local signs and exceptional representation
hypothesisChecks.statement: Let pi be cuspidal parallel weight two, omega finite-order and everywhere unramified, N its conductor, and N-prime-to-P coprime to D_(K/F). Put S equal to all real places plus the finite inert v≠P with ord_v(N) odd. The local exceptional-sign set S(chi), defined by epsilon(pi_v,chi_v)≠eta_v(−1)omega_v(−1), is S or S∪{P}; it equals S if P does not divide N, if P splits, or for sufficiently large conductor. The global sign is (−1)^|S| in those cases. Even parity is definite, odd parity indefinite. The separate representation condition pi≅pi⊗eta_(K/F) is the exceptional pair excluded in the definite branch.

sources.locator: §1.1 equations (2)–(3), pp.3–4; Lemma 1.1 and Definition 1.3, p.5; convention after Definition 1.3, p.6

acceptance: When P divides N and is inert, do not extend the stabilized sign to every small conductor.
Include all real places in S.
A positive sign alone does not remove the exceptional-pair obstruction.

hypothesisChecks.title: Geometric point and period branches
hypothesisChecks.statement: Use B/F split by K and at P. In the definite case Ram(B)=S; in the indefinite case Ram(B)=S minus one real place. H is the unit group of a fixed order R, with R_P Eichler (H1), and at every ramified K/F prime Q≠P, B_Q split and R_Q maximal (H2). Good means R_P maximal, or the two maximal-order endpoints at P have distinct intersections with g_P^−1 K_P g_P (equivalently the source conjugation convention). The indefinite quotient is a nonzero, P-new, Pic(O_F)-equivariant rational quotient J→A with A{omega_A} nonzero and projector torsion type xi_0|G_2=omega_A^epsilon for the fixed Shimura reciprocity sign epsilon. Apply the projection to alpha=q composed with the rational Hodge embedding. In the automorphic specialization epsilon=1 and omega_A=omega; the analytic chi_0 of H2 is the inverse of xi_0, since CV averages with chi and projects to chi-inverse. For each good CM point of every sufficiently large conductor, a primitive fixed-type character projection is nonzero after tensoring with the character field. The definite version uses a nonzero P-new automorphic vector in a nonexceptional representation, and has nonzero primitive-character period. Neither assertion is a statement about nonzero torsion points.

hypothesisChecks.title: Analytic branches after geometric nonvanishing
hypothesisChecks.statement: With H2 data and admissible chi_0 fixed, definite nonexceptional pi gives, for every n sufficiently large, some chi in P(n,chi_0) with L(pi,chi,1/2) nonzero, using the toric period criterion at stabilized sign. The indefinite derivative theorem in this manuscript additionally requires omega=1 and N, D_(K/F), P pairwise coprime; then for every sufficiently large n some such chi has L-prime(pi,chi,1/2) nonzero. Those extra restrictions belong to the available generalized Gross–Zagier formula, not to the geometric point theorem. The old HE.8c-prefixed indefinite target is retained with its existing mathematical parent HE.8.

hypothesisChecks.title: Dynamical supplier required by both CV branches
hypothesisChecks.statement: For the actual simultaneous reduction map Red and norm-component map C, CV dynamics takes auxiliary sets of finite primes away from P, with B_v split, K_v a field and |S_aux|+|Ram_f(B)|+[F:Q] even, and a finite nonempty set of Galois shifts pairwise distinct modulo P-rational elements rec_K(lambda) with lambda_P in K^×F_P^×. Along a P-isogeny class, compact-open Galois averages converge to the invariant probability measures on the allowed component fibres. At finite level, outside a finite exceptional set, Red(Gx)=C^−1(G C(Red(x))). This needs non-Archimedean uniform distribution on products of cocompact SL_2(F_P) quotients, including twisted-diagonal stabilizers and the commensurability criterion. Real Ratner results do not supply it. The U-commensurability criterion compares Gamma with u^−1 Gamma-prime u for some u in U, correcting the omitted prime in Definition 2.33 (E11).

hypothesisChecks.title: BCGS rational conditional nonvanishing
hypothesisChecks.statement: E/Q has conductor N, p is odd of good ordinary reduction, K is imaginary quadratic with signed d_K<0 odd and not −3, every prime dividing N splits, E(K)[p]=0, and p splits as v v-bar. With the actual Tate lattice and finite derivative system fixed, BCGS Theorem A assumes the rational anticyclotomic Greenberg main conjecture. It concludes that some squarefree product n of allowed inert Kolyvagin primes has kappa_n nonzero; kappa_1 may vanish and analytic rank one is not assumed. The proof only needs the lower divisibility L_BDP^2 divides a characteristic generator in Lambda^ur[1/p].

acceptance: Do not infer kappa_1 nonzero from nontriviality of the whole system.

hypothesisChecks.title: Main-conjecture coefficients and branch discharge
hypothesisChecks.statement: For Gamma=Gal(K_infinity/K), Lambda=Z_p[[Gamma]], Lambda^ur=Lambda completed-tensor Z_p^ur, let X_Gr be the Pontryagin dual for local conditions (0,unrestricted) at the chosen split primes. BCGS integral equality is char_Lambda(X_Gr)Lambda^ur=(L_BDP^2); rational equality is in Lambda^ur[1/p]. BCS and CGS use a single-power name for the squared BDP function; compare generated ideals after matching periods, Euler factors and local conditions. BCS Theorems 1.2.2/1.2.4 supply rational Heegner and Greenberg equalities for p>3 and E[p] irreducible over G_Q; their stated integral branch has residual surjectivity over G_Q. CGS Theorem C supplies an independent Eisenstein equality for a rational p-isogeny with kernel F_p(phi), p not dividing 2N, and phi|G_p distinct from 1 and the mod-p cyclotomic character. All field and ordinary assumptions of BCGS A remain in its application; HE.8b performs the adapters.

hypothesisChecks.title: Refined finite-system index and p-optimality
hypothesisChecks.statement: For each allowed squarefree n, I_n=p^M(n)Z_p with M(n)=min_(ell|n){v_p(a_ell),v_p(ell+1)}, M(1)=infinity and I_1=0. Put ind(0)=infinity and ind(kappa_n)=max{r:kappa_n lies in p^r H^1(K,T/I_nT)} for a nonzero class. M_r is the infimum at exactly r prime factors; M_infinity is inf_r M_r. BCGS Theorem B assumes all Theorem A data, p>3, residual G_Q→GL_2(F_p) surjective, the integral main conjecture and a fixed p-optimal modular parametrization. Then M_infinity=sum_(ell|N) v_p(c_ell(E/Q)), half the sum over K-primes above N. p-optimal means minimal p-adic valuation of the parametrization degree over the entire Q-isogeny class. M_infinity need not equal the bottom index or a Sha order.

Remove incoming HE.8/HE.8b bookkeeping edges rather than treating hypothesis checking as a theorem prerequisite. Preserve the legacy HE.8c/cornut-vatsal-nonvanishing-with-its-exact-hypotheses identifier with its existing HE.8 parent. Keep separate definite and indefinite targets, generic non-Archimedean dynamics under GN.4 or its Part II, and independent main-conjecture suppliers before HE.8b. No atlas or prior packet is edited by this job.
